report:
**Conclusion: the claim is true in the United States**, not false. Kyleena (19.5 mg levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system) is FDA-approved/indicated to prevent pregnancy **for up to five years**. The current FDA label also says it should be replaced after five years if continued contraception is wanted.

**Evidence behind the five-year duration:** FDA labeling reports a contraceptive study of 1,452 generally healthy women aged 18–35. It found a first-year Pearl Index (pregnancies per 100 woman-years) of 0.16 and a cumulative five-year pregnancy rate of 1.45% (13 pregnancies; upper 95% confidence limit 2.53%). These results support high effectiveness through the labeled five-year period. The manufacturer’s HCP site reports the same study and figures.

“Up to five years” does not mean pregnancy is impossible, nor does it establish approved effectiveness *beyond* five years. It means the device is approved for contraception through that duration; removal or replacement is recommended at five years.

Sources:  
- https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/208224s005lbl.pdf  
- http://labeling.bayerhealthcare.com/html/products/pi/Kyleena_PI.pdf  
- https://www.kyleenahcp.com/about-kyleena/efficacy
